about: Required checks for a release of the Sample Grants synthetic app. Every check maps to one acceptance criterion. Every check that opens the app runs on a still chain and on a moving chain, and both runs are required. A run that does not execute every required check in every regime cannot pass. Rules marked fictitious are demo rules: no one has approved them.

checks.title: Wallet connects on the right chain
checks.criterion: After connecting, the app shows the wallet's account, the local chain, and a TEST balance equal to the balance on chain.

rule.text: The balance a user sees is the balance the chain holds.

checks.forbidden: A displayed balance that differs from the chain.

checks.title: Refused signature sends nothing
checks.criterion: When the user refuses in the wallet (code 4001), the app says so and no transaction reaches the node.

rule.text: Nothing is sent without the user's signature.

checks.forbidden: A transaction or a nonce change after a refusal.

checks.title: Wrong network blocks sending
checks.criterion: On another chain the app shows a banner and disables payment (both awaited with a deadline), a forced click sends nothing, and the banner goes after switching back.

rule.text: Payments are only sent on the intended chain.

checks.allowed: Switch back to the local chain.
checks.forbidden: A send attempt while the wallet is on another chain.

checks.title: Terms signed before the payment
checks.method: Playwright forced click, wallet call log, API
checks.criterion: Payment stays locked until the demo terms are signed, and a forced click on the locked button sends nothing; the signature precedes the transaction; the API keeps a verified record and refuses a forged one.

rule.text: Demo terms v0 must be accepted before any payment.

checks.forbidden: A payment before the terms, or an acceptance record signed by another key.

checks.title: Allowlist enforced by the contract
checks.method: Direct contract call from a non-allowlisted account (no interface: runs once)
checks.criterion: A wallet outside the allowlist calling the contract directly is reverted with NotAllowlisted and no grant is created.

rule.text: Only allowlisted wallets may open a grant.

checks.forbidden: A non-allowlisted wallet opening a grant by skipping the interface.

checks.title: Reverted payment is shown as failed
checks.method: Playwright, fixed gas limit, direct chain reads
checks.criterion: With an empty TEST balance and a fixed gas limit, the transaction is mined with status 0, token balances do not move, the native balance drops by the fee only, and the app says failed.

rule.text: A failed payment is never presented as done.

checks.allowed: A mined, reverted transaction that costs gas.
checks.forbidden: Moved tokens or a success message after a revert.

checks.title: Nothing on the page says confirmed before the block
checks.method: Playwright, a payment held 15 s in the mempool before its block (15 empty blocks pass on the moving chain), direct chain reads
checks.criterion: With a healthy RPC, the payment waits 15 s in the mempool. Nothing on the page (status line, any other text, tab title, dialog) says confirmed before the block that holds it; then the receipt is status 1, 25 TEST move once, the grant is active on chain and the API agrees.

rule.text: Confirmed means included in a block.

checks.allowed: Pending while the transaction waits, however long and however many blocks pass.
checks.forbidden: Confirmed anywhere on the page before the block that holds the payment, or an API that disagrees with the chain.

checks.title: No confirmed without a receipt during an RPC outage
checks.method: RPC proxy cuts receipts on the app's path for at least 15 s after the payment reaches the mempool and 5 s after the screen settles; full history of the status line, state and visible text
checks.criterion: While receipt requests from the app are cut, the screen never shows the word confirmed: no receipt exists, the payment is still in the mempool. Once the bench restores the RPC and mines, both versions end on Confirmed, so only the history can tell them apart.

rule.text: Confirmed means included in a block.

checks.allowed: Pending or status unknown, then Confirmed after the block.
checks.forbidden: Confirmed at any moment while no receipt exists.

checks.title: One order, at most one debit
checks.method: RPC proxy outage; retry, Pay during unknown, reload, second device, double click, wallet error after broadcast; each pay-again done while the first payment waits and again after it landed; waits with a deadline; direct block and mempool scan; direct contract calls
checks.criterion: An order is one payer granting one reader one dataset for one access period. After status unknown, the retry looks up the same transaction again, sends nothing new, and the screen ends on Confirmed. Pay during unknown, reload then Pay, Pay from a second device, a double click, and Pay again after the wallet broadcast the payment then answered an error each move 25 TEST once, whether the user acts while the first payment waits or after it landed; on the moving chain blocks pass while the order is unpaid, and once the first payment landed the chain clock moves 40 days before the second device opens. A duplicate that the contract reverts is listed and not counted as a debit. Once the first payment is in a block, a Pay sends nothing, and after a wallet error the screen says Already paid. Straight on the contract, a paid order sent again is refused with OrderAlreadyPaid and an id that is not the open order with NotCurrentOrder. Every wait has a deadline: a slow but correct app passes, a passed deadline makes the run Incomplete.

rule.text: One order, at most one debit.

checks.allowed: Check the same transaction again. While the first payment waits, a duplicate that the contract reverts: it costs gas and moves no TEST.
checks.forbidden: A second debit for the same order, in any of the pay-again situations this check runs.

checks.title: Admin function enforced by the contract
checks.method: Direct contract calls from an allowlisted ordinary account, then from the admin
checks.criterion: The admin control is hidden for ordinary users and shown to the admin; an allowlisted ordinary account calling setAllowlisted directly, to add or to remove, is reverted with NotAdmin and the allowlist does not change; the admin can still add and remove.

rule.text: Only the admin edits the allowlist.

checks.forbidden: Any other account adding or removing an address by calling the contract.

checks.title: Revoked access is refused once indexed
checks.method: Playwright revoke held 3 s in the mempool before its block, indexer catch-up, API requests; the reader's identity is simulated by a request header
checks.criterion: With the reader's identity simulated by a request header (the demo has no reader sign-in), the API serves the dataset to the granted reader only, and refuses it once the revocation is mined and indexed.

rule.text: Revoked access ends once the revocation is indexed.

checks.allowed: Read while the grant is active.
checks.forbidden: Serving the data after the revocation is mined and indexed.

not_covered.item: Real wallet extensions and mobile wallets
not_covered.why: The bench drives an EIP-1193 test provider. It exercises the app's logic, not compatibility with MetaMask, Rabby, WalletConnect or a phone wallet.

I1 covers the status line, the rest of the status card, every other visible text on the page, the tab title and alert or confirm dialogs. Browser or system notifications, sounds, and the wallet's own popups are not observed.

not_covered.item: A duplicate sent while the first payment still waits, from a device that does not know about it
not_covered.why: The order id comes from the contract, so a second device, a cleared or refused browser storage, or a Pay after a wallet error sends the same order id, and the contract refuses a second debit of it in every case C09 runs. What a dApp without a server cannot prevent is the duplicate itself: a device that has never seen the first payment, asked while that payment is not yet in a block, sends a second transaction, which the contract reverts at the cost of its gas. Refused storage takes the same path as the second device without being run on its own.
The reader's identity is simulated: the API trusts the address declared in a request header. C11 shows that the API applies the grant state to that identity, not that the caller owns it.

not_covered.item: Economic and security audit of the contract
not_covered.why: The checks exercise three rules the contract enforces on its own (allowlist, admin role, at most one debit per order). They are not an audit: no fuzzing, no invariant testing, no review of upgrade or oracle risk.

not_covered.item: Gas spikes and congestion on a public network
not_covered.why: On the moving chain a payment waits in the mempool while empty blocks pass, as an outbid transaction would; real fee markets, replaced or cancelled transactions are not exercised.
Confirmed here means included in one block. A block that is later dropped is not simulated.

not_covered.item: Legal drafting of the terms and the allowlist
not_covered.why: The rules are fictitious demo rules. The bench checks that the app enforces them, not that they are the right rules.

not_covered.item: Load, many users at once, indexer restarts
not_covered.why: Each check runs one user on a fresh chain snapshot.

invariants.applies_to: every check that opens the app, in both regimes: all but C05
invariants.text: Nothing on the page says Confirmed too early. On the status line, not before the block that holds the receipt of the transaction it names; a status line that names no transaction (Already paid) is judged like the rest of the page. Anywhere else on the page (every other visible text, the rest of the status card included, the tab title, alert and confirm dialogs), not while a transaction of the same account, sent from any tab, is still outside a block. There the bench cannot tell which transaction a sentence means, so it judges the moment: a fact already in a block (a grant listed from the indexer, an order already paid) may say confirmed, and so may a sentence said while nothing of the account waits. The test wallet sends each change to the bench as it happens, on every tab and across reloads; the bench notes the time of each block just before mining it. A sentence that says the opposite or the future ("not confirmed", "will be confirmed once it is in a block") is not a claim.

One order, at most one debit, in each of the eleven pay-again situations C09 runs: blocks passing while the order is unpaid, a second device opened 40 days later on the chain clock, reloads, a double click and wallet errors. The order id comes from the contract (payer, reader, dataset, access period); in the contract code it depends on no block number, no time and no count of payments, and the contract refuses a second debit of it.

Every appearance the bench expects (a state, a button, a banner, the indexer) is awaited until a deadline; a passed deadline makes the run Incomplete, never Blocked. The only fixed windows are observation windows (15 s before a payment's block in C07 and C08, 3 s before the revocation's block in C11, 0.5 to 1 s after a click), and what follows them only checks that something did not happen.

regimes.title: Still chain
regimes.text: The bench mines a block only when the check decides: the moment between sent and in a block is held as long as the check needs.

regimes.title: Moving chain
regimes.text: A block every second while the user acts, and one more just before every page load, reload and click. The blocks are empty: a payment waits in the mempool, known to the node, until the check lets it into a block, as a transaction does on a busy chain. So blocks keep coming while a payment waits, during an outage, between two devices and between two clicks.
